title: The Bottle Hook: Gatorade introduces an innovation designed to help make hydration more accessible at Fuel Tomorrow Football Day of Play
summary: Created with input from adaptive athletes and Move United, Gatorade’s new Bottle Hook helps make hydration more accessible to athletes.
body_markdown:
Athletes at the Gatorade Fuel Tomorrow Football Day of Play were the first to experience the new Bottle Hook hydration innovation, alongside special guest appearances by Arizona Cardinals legend Patrick Walker, Cardinals cheerleaders and mascot, the[Cardinals Wheelchair Football Team](https://ability360.org/sports/wheelchair-football/) and Diana Flores, Gatorade athlete, two-time flag football world champion and NFL and International Federation of American Football (IFAF) Global Flag Ambassador.


“From the field to the sidelines, everyone deserves the opportunity to play, compete and have the support they need to go for it,” said Flores. “Gatorade Fuel Tomorrow Football Day of Play is about celebrating what’s possible when we create more opportunities for everyone to be part of the game.”


## Innovation shaped by adaptive athletes


The Gatorade Bottle Hook can help support autonomy and remove barriers to hydration by enabling more athletes to access hydration more independently, confidently and consistently. According to Merry, throughout the product development “they \[worked\] directly with our community, as stakeholders, as voices. \[They asked\] us, what do you need in the hydration section of your sport performance? How do we engage you differently? What tool is missing that would help you?” Through including adaptive athletes in the testing of prototypes, asking the right questions, listening to and implementing their feedback, Gatorade “developed a product that's truly unique,” said Merry. Athletes Danielle Kanas, Will Mathis and Max Richardson, who participated in the research and development process, have already noticed a difference after using the Bottle Hook.


The Gatorade Bottle Hook helps Kanas, a track-and-field athlete who competes in shot put and javelin and is a below-the-elbow left arm amputee, pick up a bottle with her left arm, something she’s never been able to do before. “It wasn’t until I used this that I really found something I would use,” she said.


It also supports Mathis by helping him stay hydrated on the green. As a blind and visually impaired golfer, Mathis says he loves the strap, adding, “It’s very easy to find and access. The tactile component of the handle allows me to orient the bottle in space.”


Richardson, a wheelchair shot putter, has arthrogryposis, which causes hand dexterity and strength challenges, called the Gatorade Bottle Hook a “life-changing accessory,” sharing that he’s “drinking more and staying hydrated more independently.”


Thanks to the Gatorade equipment design team and input from adaptive athletes, the student-athletes attending the Gatorade Fuel Tomorrow Football Day of Play were able to access hydration more independently using the Bottle Hook.
